newsitem.title: USA: U.S layoffs up 33.9 pct March vs March '96 -- report.
newsitem.headline: U.S layoffs up 33.9 pct March vs March '96 -- report.

text.p: U.S. layoffs totaled 50,182 in March, up 33.9 percent from the 37,486 job cuts announced in March 1996, according to a report by Challenger, Gray & Christmas Inc.
The March headline figure represents a 24 percent increase over the 40,480 layoffs announced in February, it said.
"March was the largest job-cut month since January, 1996," the international outplacement firm said, referring to the 97,379 jobs cut then.

About 134,257 jobs were slashed during the first quarter of 1997, 17 percent more than the fourth quarter of 1996, Challenger said. But the 1997 quarter was down 20.4 percent compared to the first quarter of 1996, which included the large AT&T Corp layoffs, it said.

"We are no longer seeing the blockbuster cuts in the tens of thousands that cause big headlines," said John Challenger, executive vice president of Challenger, Gray & Christmas. "Instead, we are seeing cuts of 2,500, 3,000 and 5,000," he said.

The leading industry sectors with the most job cuts include, the aerospace-defense (5,694), computer (4,897), financial (4,645), retail (4,366), transportation (4,188), automotive (4,098), services (3,600), industrial goods (3,540), consumer goods (3,523), and food (3,340).

"Last month's figure may be evidence that the Federal Reserve Board may have jumped the gun in raising interest rates, perhaps not taking into full account the measures companies are taking to self-correct," Challenger said.
Many companies fear inflation as much as Fed Chairman Alan Greenspan, "because they know that if they try to pass on higher costs to customers they will be eaten alive by competition," he said.
